full_text_en:
Regardless of what it’s called, we’re clearly moving to yet another era of AI agents in our work. 

We’ve quickly jumped from agents that spit out a quick answer for you, to today agents that you orchestrate inside of a set of tasks. But as agents can both fan out and work in parallel, handle much larger context, be able to do long running work, and have far greater levels of capabilities, we’re entering yet another level of what we can have AI do for us.

We’ll soon be able to give agents a set of goals, and they can go out and design the best solution for that goal, while also continuously improving it based on the ongoing execution of whatever it built. This will obviously start with engineering because that’s where we’re seeing the best practices emerge first in almost every new era of agents. 

But the impact can be quite massive across the rest of knowledge work. You’ll tell an agent to improve your client onboarding workflow to achieve a certain targeted goal; or have agents go reduce risk in your business; or improve your security posture on an ongoing basis.

These autonomous systems will be able to take on a set of goals, design the best outcome, test and iterate, deploy, and then optimize whatever it built on an ongoing basis. Importantly, this leads to outcomes and results that humans literally couldn’t have accomplished before. This will lead to fairly new levels of productivity with AI.
full_text_zh:
不管它叫什么，我们的工作显然正在进入人工智能代理的另一个时代。

我们很快就从为您提供快速答案的代理跃升至今天您在一组任务中编排的代理。但是，由于智能体既可以扇出并并行工作，可以处理更大的环境，能够进行长时间运行的工作，并且具有更高水平的功能，我们正在进入人工智能为我们做的事情的另一个层面。

我们很快就能够为代理提供一组目标，他们可以出去设计实现该目标的最佳解决方案，同时还可以根据其所构建的内容的持续执行不断改进它。显然，这将从工程开始，因为我们看到几乎每个新代理时代都首先出现最佳实践。

但对其他知识工作的影响可能相当巨大。您将告诉代理改进您的客户入职工作流程以实现特定的目标；或者让代理人去降低您的业务风险；或持续改善您的安全状况。

这些自主系统将能够实现一系列目标、设计最佳结果、测试和迭代、部署，然后优化其持续构建的任何内容。重要的是，这会带来人类以前根本无法实现的结果。这将导致人工智能的生产力达到新的水平。

title: Elon gave two talks today at DealBook and TomorrowX Summit, revealing more about SpaceX's plans than most earnings calls
title_en:
Elon gave two talks today at DealBook and TomorrowX Summit, revealing more about SpaceX's plans than most earnings calls. Here are the 11 key takeaways:

1. SpaceX is scaling AI compute at an extraordinary pace:

SpaceX is adding roughly 500 MW monthly, equivalent to 220,000 GB300s. Elon expects over 1 GW monthly by end-2027: a 6 GW annualized pace today, doubling to 12 GW. 

2. Its build costs are far below industry estimates:

Elon says outside estimates are off by up to 2x, with SpaceX building at roughly 60% of industry costs. Its in-house "Army X" builds the data centers, while Tesla Megapacks smooth training power. I'd already been modeling a 25–30% SpaceX cost advantage. 

3. Anthropic could become a 10 GW customer:

Anthropic told Elon its most likely outcome is renting another 10 GW from SpaceX, on top of existing capacity. Contracts allow termination with 3–6 months' notice, but Anthropic says staying is "extremely likely." This reinforces my model that Anthropic will take most upcoming capacity.

4. SpaceX is targeting a vastly larger telecom market:

Elon argues AT&T and Verizon won't disappear as bandwidth demand explodes. Humans communicate at roughly 100 bits per second, while superintelligence and robots could require a trillion. SpaceX is targeting a market orders of magnitude larger than existing telecom revenue, as I'd modeled. Even more interestingly, this creates an opportunity to push its AI business further.

5. Its next-generation satellite network arrives next year:

Direct to Cell V2 launches with 40x V1's bandwidth. Micro cell towers using 800 MHz and rooftop units resembling Starlink dishes will extend indoor coverage, with rooftop hardware entering production next year. Starlink is becoming a full scale carrier. 

6. SpaceXSI has rebuilt its entire AI software stack:

Over six to eight months, it rewrote training, reinforcement learning, and inference from scratch, close to the metal in C and C++. Elon thinks it "might have the best training stack software in the world." Grok 4.8 is also being built for practical usefulness rather than benchmark leadership, which is great for Grokbot.

7. Terafab could become the largest project on Earth:

The facility is planned to reach 100 million square feet, with phase-one volume production targeted for late 2028. Elon says established chipmakers are risk-averse because of massive capex, while SpaceX will take risks and iterate rapidly toward a better chip process by 2028.

8. Optimus is moving toward industrial work:

Elon expects an unstaged demonstration in a month or two and says Optimus could do dishes within 12–18 months. Its first major industrial role will be mining and refining ore for national security.

9. A Tesla–SpaceX merger is becoming increasingly logical:

Elon says the companies are "probably" better together as AI and robotics bring them closer. Both have AI software teams and advanced chip-design capabilities, while superintelligence compute could eventually move into orbit. Shareholders will decide; Elon says he shouldn't receive an award simply for merging them.

10. Ship 42 could accelerate the entire Starship reuse program:

Ship 42 needed only minor repairs before flying again, but SpaceX is retiring it for public display. This brings rapid reuse much closer.

11. SpaceX is targeting 200 GW of annual solar manufacturing for space:

That's roughly 40% of average US electricity consumption. Its Starmind compute unit delivers the same capability at roughly a quarter the size of a Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, which is a win in space. Elon says it's also simpler than Starlink V3, which is already in production.

Simply put, SpaceX is building toward a trillion-dollar annual revenue business within just a few years, at scale never seen before.

Many of these numbers I've already modeled and shared over the past few months. Yesterday's announcements bring those projections closer to reality.

The scale of what's coming is extraordinary!

SpaceX is adding roughly 500 MW monthly, equivalent to 220,000 GB300s. Elon expects over 1 GW monthly by end-2027: a 6 GW annualized pace today, doubling to 12 GW. 

2. Its build costs are far below industry estimates:

Elon says outside estimates are off by up to 2x, with SpaceX building at roughly 60% of industry costs. Its in-house "Army X" builds the data centers, while Tesla Megapacks smooth training power. I'd already been modeling a 25–30% SpaceX cost advantage. 

3. Anthropic could become a 10 GW customer:

Anthropic told Elon its most likely outcome is renting another 10 GW from SpaceX, on top of existing capacity. Contracts allow termination with 3–6 months' notice, but Anthropic says staying is "extremely likely." This reinforces my model that Anthropic will take most upcoming capacity.

4. SpaceX is targeting a vastly larger telecom market:

Elon argues AT&T and Verizon won't disappear as bandwidth demand explodes. Humans communicate at roughly 100 bits per second, while superintelligence and robots could require a trillion. SpaceX is targeting a market orders of magnitude larger than existing telecom revenue, as I'd modeled. Even more interestingly, this creates an opportunity to push its AI business further.

5. Its next-generation satellite network arrives next year:

Direct to Cell V2 launches with 40x V1's bandwidth. Micro cell towers using 800 MHz and rooftop units resembling Starlink dishes will extend indoor coverage, with rooftop hardware entering production next year. Starlink is becoming a full scale carrier. 

6. SpaceXSI has rebuilt its entire AI software stack:

Over six to eight months, it rewrote training, reinforcement learning, and inference from scratch, close to the metal in C and C++. Elon thinks it "might have the best training stack software in the world." Grok 4.8 is also being built for practical usefulness rather than benchmark leadership, which is great for Grokbot.

7. Terafab could become the largest project on Earth:

The facility is planned to reach 100 million square feet, with phase-one volume production targeted for late 2028. Elon says established chipmakers are risk-averse because of massive capex, while SpaceX will take risks and iterate rapidly toward a better chip process by 2028.

8. Optimus is moving toward industrial work:

Elon expects an unstaged demonstration in a month or two and says Optimus could do dishes within 12–18 months. Its first major industrial role will be mining and refining ore for national security.

9. A Tesla–SpaceX merger is becoming increasingly logical:

Elon says the companies are "probably" better together as AI and robotics bring them closer. Both have AI software teams and advanced chip-design capabilities, while superintelligence compute could eventually move into orbit. Shareholders will decide; Elon says he shouldn't receive an award simply for merging them.

10. Ship 42 could accelerate the entire Starship reuse program:

Ship 42 needed only minor repairs before flying again, but SpaceX is retiring it for public display. This brings rapid reuse much closer.

11. SpaceX is targeting 200 GW of annual solar manufacturing for space:

That's roughly 40% of average US electricity consumption. Its Starmind compute unit delivers the same capability at roughly a quarter the size of a Vera Rubin NVL72 rack, which is a win in space. Elon says it's also simpler than Starlink V3, which is already in production.

Simply put, SpaceX is building toward a trillion-dollar annual revenue business within just a few years, at scale never seen before.

Many of these numbers I've already modeled and shared over the past few months. Yesterday's announcements bring those projections closer to reality.

The scale of what's coming is extraordinary!
full_text_zh:
埃隆今天在 DealBook 和 TomorrowX 峰会上发表了两场演讲，比大多数财报电话会议透露了更多有关 SpaceX 计划的内容。以下是 11 个要点：

1. SpaceX 正在以惊人的速度扩展人工智能计算：

SpaceX 每月增加约 500 MW，相当于 220,000 个 GB300。 Elon 预计，到 2027 年底，每月装机容量将超过 1 吉瓦：目前年化装机容量为 6 吉瓦，翻倍至 12 吉瓦。

2. 其建造成本远低于业界预估：

埃隆表示，外界估计的成本高达 2 倍，SpaceX 的建设成本约为行业成本的 60%。其内部的“Army X”负责构建数据中心，而 Tesla Megapacks 则负责平稳的训练能力。我已经对 SpaceX 的成本优势进行了 25-30% 的建模。

3. Anthropic 可能成为 10 GW 客户：

Anthropic 告诉 Elon，最有可能的结果是在现有产能的基础上，再从 SpaceX 租用 10 GW 的产能。合同允许提前 3 至 6 个月通知终止，但 Anthropic 表示留下来“极有可能”。这强化了我的模型，即 Anthropic 将承担大部分即将到来的容量。

4. SpaceX 的目标是更大的电信市场：

埃隆认为 AT&T 和 Verizon 不会随着带宽需求的爆炸式增长而消失。人类的通信速度约为每秒 100 比特，而超级智能和机器人可能需要每秒 1 万亿比特。正如我所建模的，SpaceX 的目标是比现有电信收入大几个数量级的市场。更有趣的是，这为进一步推动其人工智能业务创造了机会。

5. 其下一代卫星网络将于明年到来：

Direct to Cell V2 推出，带宽是 V1 的 40 倍。使用 800 MHz 的微型蜂窝塔和类似于星链天线的屋顶单元将扩大室内覆盖范围，屋顶硬件将于明年投入生产。星链正在成为一家全面的运营商。

6. SpaceXSI 重建了整个人工智能软件堆栈：

在六到八个月的时间里，它从头开始重写了训练、强化学习和推理，接近 C 和 C++ 中的金属。埃隆认为它“可能拥有世界上最好的训练堆栈软件”。 Grok 4.8 的构建也是为了实用性而不是基准领导力，这对 Grokbot 来说非常好。

7. Terafab 可能成为地球上最大的项目：

该工厂计划面积达到 1 亿平方英尺，一期批量生产目标为 2028 年末。Elon 表示，成熟的芯片制造商由于巨额资本支出而不愿承担风险，而 SpaceX 将承担风险并快速迭代，到 2028 年实现更好的芯片工艺。

8. Optimus 正在走向工业工作：

Elon 预计在一两个月内进行一次非现场演示，并表示 Optimus 可以在 12 至 18 个月内完成洗碗。其第一个主要工业角色将是为国家安全开采和提炼矿石。

9. 特斯拉与 SpaceX 的合并变得越来越合乎逻辑：

埃隆表示，随着人工智能和机器人技术拉近了两家公司的距离，两家公司“可能”会更好地合作。两者都拥有人工智能软件团队和先进的芯片设计能力，而超级智能计算最终可能会进入轨道。股东将决定；埃隆说他不应该仅仅因为合并它们而获得奖项。

10. 42 号船可以加速整个星舰再利用计划：

42 号飞船在再次飞行之前只需要进行小修，但 SpaceX 正在将其退役以供公开展示。这使得快速重用更加接近。

11. SpaceX 的目标是每年制造 200 吉瓦的太空太阳能：

这大约相当于美国平均用电量的 40%。其 Starmind 计算单元提供相同的功能，尺寸约为 Vera Rubin NVL72 机架的四分之一，这在空间上是一个胜利。 Elon 表示，它也比已经投入生产的 Starlink V3 更简单。

简而言之，SpaceX 正在短短几年内打造年收入数万亿美元的业务，规模前所未见。

在过去的几个月里，我已经对其中的许多数字进行了建模和分享。昨天的公告使这些预测更接近现实。

即将发生的事情的规模是非同寻常的！

title:
Guys, I want to share share from my recent experience in AI/ML:

- Do not chase every AI trend

- Make every project end
title_en:
Guys, I want to share share from my recent experience in AI/ML:

- Do not chase every AI trend

- Make every project end-to-end

- Learn high-level ML system design

- When explaining a project, cover: business, data pipeline, model/agent, eval, deployment, and numerical results

- Never let coding agents run commands themselves; get the commands and run them yourself

- When vibe coding, always check results against expectations

- Avoid overcomplicating projects with fancy tools

- Companies care about impact, not your tech stack

- Interviewers want what you know, not buzzwords

- MLOps is a necessity; there is no specialized ML role now

- Airflow, MLflow, Linux basics, Docker, CI/CD, Terraform, and Redis are important

- Automate low-level coding and analysis with LLMs, with a human in the loop

- Bash, YAML, Markdown, and JSON are 90% of engineering today and the entry point to every project

- Understand the business so you can automate QA and iteratively build better solutions

- GraphRAG is the most important part to learn today

- Designing ETL pipelines is smart work that impacts the whole project

- Basics save you when models or agents fail in production

- Code everything with AI, but understand each stage and ask cross-questions on the solutions

Most important: Companies treat AI, ML, MLOps, and data under one department. The more you know, the more you grow.

There is no excuse. Learn all parts and use AI to code.
title_zh:
各位，我想分享一下我最近在 AI/ML 方面的经验：

- 不要追逐每一个人工智能趋势

- 使每个项目端到端

- 学习高级机器学习系统设计

- 在解释项目时，涵盖：业务、数据管道、模型/代理、评估、部署和数值结果

- 切勿让编码代理
full_text_en:
Guys, I want to share share from my recent experience in AI/ML:

- Do not chase every AI trend

- Make every project end-to-end

- Learn high-level ML system design

- When explaining a project, cover: business, data pipeline, model/agent, eval, deployment, and numerical results

- Never let coding agents run commands themselves; get the commands and run them yourself

- When vibe coding, always check results against expectations

- Avoid overcomplicating projects with fancy tools

- Companies care about impact, not your tech stack

- Interviewers want what you know, not buzzwords

- MLOps is a necessity; there is no specialized ML role now

- Airflow, MLflow, Linux basics, Docker, CI/CD, Terraform, and Redis are important

- Automate low-level coding and analysis with LLMs, with a human in the loop

- Bash, YAML, Markdown, and JSON are 90% of engineering today and the entry point to every project

- Understand the business so you can automate QA and iteratively build better solutions

- GraphRAG is the most important part to learn today

- Designing ETL pipelines is smart work that impacts the whole project

- Basics save you when models or agents fail in production

- Code everything with AI, but understand each stage and ask cross-questions on the solutions

Most important: Companies treat AI, ML, MLOps, and data under one department. The more you know, the more you grow.

There is no excuse. Learn all parts and use AI to code.
full_text_zh:
各位，我想分享一下我最近在 AI/ML 方面的经验：

- 不要追逐每一个人工智能趋势

- 使每个项目端到端

- 学习高级机器学习系统设计

- 在解释项目时，涵盖：业务、数据管道、模型/代理、评估、部署和数值结果

- 切勿让编码代理自行运行命令；获取命令并自行运行

- 当氛围编码时，始终根据预期检查结果

- 避免使用花哨的工具使项目过于复杂

- 公司关心影响力，而不是你的技术堆栈

- 面试官想要的是你所知道的，而不是流行语

- MLOps 是必需品；现在没有专门的机器学习角色

- Airflow、MLflow、Linux 基础知识、Docker、CI/CD、Terraform 和 Redis 很重要

- 通过法学硕士实现低级编码和分析的自动化，并由人员参与

- Bash、YAML、Markdown 和 JSON 是当今 90% 的工程，也是每个项目的入口点

- 了解业务，以便您可以自动化 QA 并迭代构建更好的解决方案

- GraphRAG是今天要学习的最重要的部分

- 设计 ETL 管道是影响整个项目的明智工作

- 当模型或代理在生产中失败时，基础知识可以拯救你

- 使用人工智能对所有内容进行编码，但了解每个阶段并就解决方案提出交叉问题

最重要的是：公司将 AI、ML、MLOps 和数据归入一个部门。你知道的越多，你成长的就越多。

没有任何借口。学习所有部件并使用人工智能进行编码。

title:
good morning everyone 💜

what if computing power didn't have to come from a handful of large data centers?

recent cloud
title_en:
good morning everyone 💜

what if computing power didn't have to come from a handful of large data centers?

recent cloud disruptions on November 12–13 affected Microsoft services like Outlook, Teams and Copilot across 74 countries.

incidents like this make me think about how much of our digital activity depends on centralized infrastructure.

this is one reason @Acurast caught my attention.

instead of putting all computing capacity in centralized data centers, Acurast takes a distributed approach by turning smartphones into independent Processors.

and the scale is worth noticing:

→ 360K+ phones across 175+ countries
→ 770K+ compute deployments
→ 1.1B+ on-chain transactions

but the interesting part isn't just the number of connected devices.

how can people actually participate?

Acurast offers two options:

• Processor Lite allows compatible Android phones and iPhones to contribute computing power.

• Processor Core is designed for dedicated Android devices.

developers can distribute workloads across different Processors, while hardware-backed attestation helps verify the code running on participating devices.

this opens up possibilities for AI agents, monitoring systems and failover services that need alternatives to relying on a single cloud provider.

of course, Acurast isn't a direct replacement for services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook.

i see its potential in creating another layer of decentralized computing infrastructure.

and perhaps one of the most interesting parts is that an ordinary compatible smartphone can become part of that infrastructure.

exploring this side of @Acurast makes the project even more interesting to follow.

full_text_zh:
大家早上好💜

如果计算能力不必来自少数大型数据中心怎么办？

最近 11 月 12 日至 13 日发生的云中断影响了 74 个国家/地区的 Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 等 Microsoft 服务。

此类事件让我思考我们的数字活动在多大程度上依赖于集中式基础设施。

这是@Acurast 引起我注意的原因之一。

Acurast 没有将所有计算能力放在集中式数据中心，而是采用分布式方法，将智能手机转变为独立的处理器。

规模值得注意：

→ 超过 175 个国家/地区的 36 万多部手机
→ 770K+ 计算部署
→ 1.1B+链上交易

但有趣的部分不仅仅是连接设备的数量。

人们如何真正参与？

Acurast 提供两种选择：

• Processor Lite 允许兼容的Android 手机和iPhone 贡献计算能力。

• 处理器核心专为专用Android 设备而设计。

开发人员可以在不同的处理器上分配工作负载，而硬件支持的证明有助于验证参与设备上运行的代码。

这为人工智能代理、监控系统和故障转移服务提供了可能性，这些服务需要替代方案来依赖单一云提供商。

当然，Acurast 并不是 Microsoft Teams 或 Outlook 等服务的直接替代品。

我看到了它在创建另一层去中心化计算基础设施方面的潜力。

也许最有趣的部分之一是普通的兼容智能手机可以成为该基础设施的一部分。

探索 @Acurast 的这一面使该项目变得更加有趣。

title:
What if SEO, content, ads, and marketing strategy could all work together under one AI agent?

That's exactly what @zavi
title_en:
What if SEO, content, ads, and marketing strategy could all work together under one AI agent?

That's exactly what @zaviagent is building.

Zavi is an AI growth agent that analyzes your business, identifies growth opportunities, builds strategies, and helps execute them across different channels.

From SEO and AEO/GEO to content, social media, email marketing, paid ads, performance tracking, and workflow automation, it brings multiple growth activities into one place.

I tested @zaviagent Business Analysis and SEO/GEO features, and I like how they identify growth opportunities, highlight visibility issues, and suggest actionable improvements. 
Instead of just giving generic advice, Zavi helps turn insights into a practical growth plan.

It's particularly useful for founders, startups, small businesses, and lean marketing teams who don't have the time, resources, or personnel to manage every growth channel themselves.

Of course, AI doesn't guarantee growth, and its recommendations still need human judgment. But having an agent that can analyze, plan, execute, and monitor instead of simply generating suggestions is a meaningful step forward.

I recommend using this AI agent if you're looking to simplify your marketing workflow and spend less time juggling tools.

The real value isn't just having AI. It's having AI that can actually do the work.

title: When you work with AI, you get faster results, quicker deliveries, and improved productivity, especially as a programmer
title_en:
When you work with AI, you get faster results, quicker deliveries, and improved productivity, especially as a programmer. But there's a downside that many people seem to overlook: you gradually become too dependent on AI and stop exercising your own critical thinking skills.

That's where the real problem begins. Many programmers today are becoming so dependent on AI and vibe coding that they struggle to write code independently, even though they knew how to code before AI became popular.

Imagine having no internet access or attending a job interview where you're expected to demonstrate your coding skills without AI. You could find yourself struggling because you've become so accustomed to letting AI do the thinking and problem-solving for you that you've neglected the skills you already had.

AI is a powerful tool, but it shouldn't replace your ability to think, learn, and solve problems independently. The real danger isn't using AI; it's becoming so dependent on it that you forget how to work without it.

That's the problem many people still don't see.

gm everyone ☀️

one thing i didn't realize at first while exploring @termix_ai is that you don't actually need to build
title_en:
gm everyone ☀️

one thing i didn't realize at first while exploring @termix_ai is that you don't actually need to build an AI agent to use its marketplace.

regular apps can also hire AI agents to get specific jobs done. and honestly i think this is one of the more interesting parts of the whole ecosystem.
let's say you're building a design application.

a user needs a logo banner or some custom graphics. instead of building every feature yourself, your app could simply find an agent that specializes in design, send it a job and receive the finished result.
that's basically what the TermiX SDK makes possible.

here's how the process works:-))

→ your app connects to the TermiX marketplace through the SDK.

→ it discovers available agent services and finds the one that matches the task.

→ your app places an order with the selected agent.

→ the payment goes into an escrow contract instead of being transferred directly.

→ the agent completes the task and submits the deliverable.

→ once the delivery process is verified, payment can be settled onchain in USDC or USDT.

another thing i like is that developers aren't restricted to a single programming language.

TermiX provides SDK support for TypeScript, Python and Go, making integration more accessible for different development teams.

but there's another detail worth mentioning: wallet control.

TermiX doesn't take custody of your private keys or sign transactions for your application.

when an action requires an onchain transaction, the backend returns an unsigned transaction. your own wallet or connected signer handles the signing and broadcasting.

so your application stays in control of its funds.

why does this actually matter?
because developers don't have to build an entire agent marketplace, payment system and escrow mechanism from scratch.
they can focus on their actual product and let specialized agents handle the additional work.

imagine a gaming platform hiring an agent to create game assets, a research app ordering market analysis, or an e-commerce platform using agents for product descriptions.

the possibilities go beyond AI assistants answering prompts.

for me the bigger idea behind @termix_ai is making AI services accessible to both agents and regular applications.

not every app needs its own AI workforce. sometimes it just needs the ability to find, hire and pay someone else's agent.

that's the kind of agent economy i'm interested in watching develop.

what's one task you'd outsource to an AI agent if your favorite app supported this today?

full_text_zh:
gm大家☀️

在探索 @termix_ai 时，我一开始没有意识到的一件事是，您实际上不需要构建人工智能代理来使用其市场。

常规应用程序还可以雇用人工智能代理来完成特定的工作。老实说，我认为这是整个生态系统中最有趣的部分之一。
假设您正在构建一个设计应用程序。

用户需要徽标横幅或一些自定义图形。您的应用程序可以简单地找到专门从事设计的代理，向其发送任务并接收最终结果，而不是自己构建每个功能。
这基本上就是 TermiX SDK 所实现的。

以下是该过程的工作原理:-))

→ 您的应用程序通过 SDK 连接到 TermiX 市场。

→ 它会发现可用的代理服务并找到与任务匹配的服务。

→ 您的应用程序向选定的代理商下订单。

→ 付款进入托管合同，而不是直接转账。

→ 代理完成任务并提交可交付成果。

→ 一旦交付过程得到验证，付款可以通过 USDC 或 USDT 进行链上结算。

我喜欢的另一件事是开发人员不限于单一编程语言。

TermiX 提供对 TypeScript、Python 和 Go 的 SDK 支持，使不同开发团队更容易集成。

但还有一个细节值得一提：钱包控制。

TermiX 不会保管您的私钥或为您的应用程序签署交易。

当操作需要链上交易时，后端返回未签名的交易。您自己的钱包或连接的签名者处理签名和广播。

这样您的应用程序就可以控制其资金。

为什么这实际上很重要？
因为开发者不必从头开始构建整个代理市场、支付系统和托管机制。
他们可以专注于自己的实际产品，并让专门的代理处理额外的工作。

想象一下一个游戏平台雇佣一个代理来创建游戏资产，一个研究应用程序订购市场分析，或者一个电子商务平台使用代理来进行产品描述。

可能性不仅仅限于人工智能助手回答提示。

对我来说，@termix_ai 背后更大的想法是让人工智能服务可供代理和常规应用程序访问。

并非每个应用程序都需要自己的人工智能劳动力。有时它只需要有能力找到、雇用和支付其他人的代理人的费用。

这就是我有兴趣观察的代理经济的发展。

如果您最喜欢的应用程序现在支持一项任务，您会外包给人工智能代理吗？

title_en:
Good morning, legends 

The real value of an AI agent isn't just what it can say. It's what it can actually get done.

We're already seeing agents handle tasks that once required direct human involvement. From making phone calls to navigating customer service conversations, their capabilities are becoming increasingly practical.

But there's another important step: turning those capabilities into economic opportunities.

That's the direction @termix_ai is exploring with Agent Skills and https://t.co/BOxbHxlLgM.

Agents can connect to a marketplace where they discover available jobs, take on bounties, complete assigned tasks, and receive payment for their work.

This changes the way we think about AI agents.

Instead of being tools that only respond when prompted, they can become active participants in a growing digital economy.

And with TermiX Agent Skills working across different agents, the opportunity isn't limited to one AI platform.

The next big step for AI isn't simply making agents smarter. It's building the infrastructure that allows them to work, collaborate, deliver value, and get paid.

Agents can do the work. TermiX is helping create the marketplace where that work has value.

title:
Imagine having an AI Agent that can do more than answer questions.

With @meetmotes, the idea is to connect each Genesis
title_en:
Imagine having an AI Agent that can do more than answer questions.

With @meetmotes, the idea is to connect each Genesis NFT to a dedicated Agent and Smart Account, giving it a defined environment to work within.

But what does user control actually look like?

Imagine funding an Agent with 1,000 USDC to manage an approved list of DeFi assets.

You could set:
→ Maximum 10% per trade
→ A daily spending cap of 300 USDC
→ Slippage limit of 0.5%
→ Borrowing disabled
→ Pause new trades if the account value falls to 850 USDC

The Agent can research and propose actions, but transactions must pass the account's policy checks before execution.

That's the important distinction: AI can make decisions, but permissions should determine what it is allowed to do.

Motes' documentation describes this architecture, including policy enforcement, execution logs, pause controls and permission revocation.

What I still want to see is the evidence in practice:

→ Verified smart-account contracts and independent security reviews
→ Onchain records showing limits enforced on every transaction
→ Execution logs covering successful, rejected and failed actions
→ A tested pause and revocation process

The concept behind $MOTES is interesting, but reliable execution and genuine owner control need to be demonstrated, not just promised.

More research to come.

这是重要的区别：人工智能可以做出决定，但权限应该决定它可以做什么。

Motes 的文档描述了这种架构，包括策略实施、执行日志、暂停控制和权限撤销。

我还想看到的是实践中的证据：

→ 经过验证的智能账户合约和独立的安全审查
→ 链上记录显示每笔交易的限制
→ 执行日志涵盖成功、拒绝和失败的操作
→ 经过测试的暂停和撤销流程

$MOTES 背后的概念很有趣，但需要证明可靠的执行和真正的所有者控制，而不仅仅是承诺。

更多研究即将到来。

title:
An AI agent can follow its budget and still look like it overspent.

Imagine a wallet showing a reserved fee as money al
title_en:
An AI agent can follow its budget and still look like it overspent.

Imagine a wallet showing a reserved fee as money already spent, then returning the unused portion later. The agent stayed within its limit. The display made it look otherwise.

Edgars Nemše's explanation of @GenLayer moving its chain from ZK Stack to @arbitrum Nitro made me think about that kind of edge case.

The protocol's judgment method did not change. Optimistic Democracy and GenVM work as before. The migration work was where contracts touch the chain: the bridge, Ethereum integration and how chain gas costs are handled.

If I were testing that move, I'd look beyond whether a transaction runs and check whether the cost shown to users tells the right story.

If an agent paid from your wallet, which number would you want to see first: the reserve, the actual cost or the refund?

That is why I’ve started paying attention to what @meetmotes  is building.

Instead of constantly checking charts, monitoring market volatility, and executing every single move myself, I can set up an AI Agent exactly the way I want.

我仍然是制定目标、策略和我愿意承担的风险水平的人。代理负责处理执行，使我不必手动管理一切。

对我来说，Motes 的价值不仅仅是拥有另一个人工智能可以与之聊天，而是将人工智能转变为能够在 DeFi 生态系统中采取行动的真正助手。

也许金融的未来不仅仅是我们为自己进行交易，而是能够将任务委托给根据我们自己的策略运作的代理。

如果您有自己的人工智能代理，您会首先给它分配什么交易策略？

The existential risk for enterp
title_en:
@ypatil125 @rythmrg @lindensli looking forward to welcoming you to Palo Alto Networks. 

The existential risk for enterprise companies is their lack of frontier level talent and the possiblity that someone reinvents our business with AI. So first and foremost the new team has a task, to ensure Palo Alto Networks is the world leader in applying frontier AI to its security portfolio and I can't think of a better person to help drive that  @ypatil125 as Co-Chief AI Officer I expect him and his team to help us transform to an AI first company. I have always maintained winning teams are humble enough to know what they can do and when they need to bring in a team to lead with them. We will be stronger and better together. 

I firmly believe that the acceleration of enterprise AI adoption will be driven by a reliable, scalable, secure implementation of open weight/source models. Upon inspection, there is not many scale players who are ready to serve this markets from ideation with customers, to training, continuous learning and partnering with secure inference providers.We think we can help the  Applied Compute team with our enterprise capabilities and deliver on this vision together. 

Lastly and equally important I believe- to provide true reliability, explanability and verifiability of AI in enterprise applications - we should be training a digital twin or "supervisory AI" which is reward hacked to observe "task AI" and alert on non compliance. It is impossible to deliver safety and security without training both models together with different objective functions. Without being able to interrogate chain of thought, we intend to work with the Applied Compute team to validate this future .

We intend to become a key player in the AI economy in engendering trust in AI so we can collectively drive Enterprise trust. 

Yes, there will be things to learn, pivot and adapt as we continue on this journey, but me and the team are excited to go after this with the @appliedcompute team. 

In times of technology inflection, if you don't act on your instinct - you lose.

full_text_zh:
@ypatil125 @rythmrg @lindensli 期待您来到 Palo Alto Networks。

企业公司的生存风险是缺乏前沿人才，以及有人利用人工智能重塑我们业务的可能性。因此，新团队的首要任务是确保 Palo Alto Networks 在将前沿人工智能应用到其安全产品组合方面处于世界领先地位，我想不出比这更好的人选了。@ypatil125 作为联合首席人工智能官，我希望他和他的团队能够帮助我们转型为人工智能优先的公司。我一直认为获胜的团队足够谦虚，知道自己能做什么，以及何时需要引入团队来领导他们。我们将一起变得更强、更好。

我坚信，开放权重/源代码模型的可靠、可扩展、安全实施将推动企业人工智能的加速采用。经过检查，没有多少规模参与者准备好服务这个市场，从与客户的构思，到培训、持续学习以及与安全推理提供商的合作。我们认为我们可以利用我们的企业能力帮助应用计算团队并共同实现这一愿景。

最后，我认为同样重要的是，为了在企业应用程序中提供人工智能的真正可靠性、可解释性和可验证性，我们应该训练一个数字孪生或“监督人工智能”，它会被奖励黑客观察“任务人工智能”并对不合规情况发出警报。如果不使用不同的目标函数对两个模型进行训练，就不可能提供安全性。在无法询问思想链的情况下，我们打算与应用计算团队合作来验证这个未来。

我们打算成为人工智能经济中建立人工智能信任的关键参与者，以便我们能够共同推动企业信任。

是的，随着我们继续这一旅程，将会有一些东西需要学习、调整和适应，但我和团队很高兴能与 @appliedcompute 团队一起追求这一目标。

在技​​术变革的时代，如果你不按照自己的直觉行事，你就会失败。

title: The New York Times just ran Anthropic's best ad of the IPO. They call it a profile. It reads like a prospectus. The auth
title_en:
The New York Times just ran Anthropic's best ad of the IPO. They call it a profile. It reads like a prospectus. The author left out who funded her reporting.

Another classic Anthropic puff piece. Receipts below.

On the surface, her pre-IPO profile of Anthropic in the New York Times lands a few soft, harmless jabs. Strip away the Silicon Valley jargon, though, and every "critique" turns into a high-end sales pitch aimed straight at "Americans' retirement portfolios." That's you.

Here are the receipts she printed, and the one she hid.

1. The "reluctant hero" trick.

After paragraphs of employees agonizing over how to "slow down A.I.," the piece admits Anthropic's #1 priority with IPO cash is buying massive compute to reach "recursive self-improvement" (AI building uncontrollable AI) before OpenAI and China.

Meanwhile, it warns about mass layoffs while being the leading seller of the AI agents that "threaten to replace white-collar workers."

It sells the flood and the sandbags.

2. The $70 billion fund, and the fine print.

The company is putting 5% of a $1.4T company ($70 billion) into a "Public Benefit Fund" for donations of its choosing. Its employees are pledging their stock to charity too.

Read her order: animal welfare, global health, AI safety. Then, last: "Many have begun giving big to political campaigns."

Charity on the label. Politics in the fine print.

Tucked between the "ascetic monk" anecdotes is the real pitch: insiders aren't selling, Claude Code "reinvented" coding, and revenue passed OpenAI.

That isn't a profile. That's a prospectus with a byline.

3. The monopoly free pass.

Anthropic is lobbying Congress for an antitrust exemption (a legal cartel), pre-empting state AI laws, and talking about becoming "more powerful than the government."

A five-tier stock structure: you buy the shares, they keep the vote.

Count the named critics in the entire piece: zero.

Even after citing examples of Claude "only pretending to follow its instructions," how does Sun let it off the hook? One magic sentence:

"I do not doubt these good intentions."

Compare how she treats regular Americans. In August, she toured the Midwest towns fighting AI data centers on their land, then filed their anger under: "'AI populism' is more about populism than about AI."

A Wisconsin town fights a data center: populism.
A trillion-dollar AI lab sells its IPO: good intentions.

The neighbors get diagnosed. The billionaires get believed.

4. The missing receipt.

The biggest conflict isn't in Anthropic's prospectus. It's in the byline.

The money: Sun's August data-center story ends: "This story was supported by a grant from the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism." Tarbell is bankrolled by Coefficient Giving, the foundation of Anthropic early investor Dustin Moskovitz.

The overlap: She wrote that her D.C. party overlapped with the Coefficient Giving team retreat: "The lines got blurry—I think my group was the intersection of both."

Her words. Not mine.

5. The hypocrisy.

On 80,000 Hours, she set the rule: "I don't think that you can do especially credible either journalistic work or policy advocacy work if you are employed by a lab: you are going to be seen as a shill. You are correctly seen as a shill."

Same show, when the money came from the lab's investors instead of the lab, she called that a witch hunt: they're "going after all the Tarbell fellows and saying these people are just Anthropic shills."

Lab paycheck: shill. Lab investor's grant: witch hunt.

Then she took a Tarbell grant herself. Then she wrote Anthropic's IPO profile in the New York Times. Then she left out the disclosure.

Her rule. Her money. Her silence.

In August, she could type the disclosure. In November, on the eve of Anthropic's IPO, she left it out.

So admit it.

You took money from Anthropic's investor network. Admit it.
You were in the room with the funders. Your words. Admit it.
You wrote their sales pitch on the eve of their IPO. Admit it.
You left out the one sentence you already know how to type. 
Admit it.

Regular Americans report every dollar to the IRS. 
You couldn't spare your readers one sentence.

By her own standard, what is she?

Who's the shill now?

Tarbell fellows?

3. The monopoly free pass.

Anthropic is lobbying Congress for an antitrust exemption (a legal cartel), pre-empting state AI laws, and talking about becoming "more powerful than the government."

A five-tier stock structure: you buy the shares, they keep the vote.

Count the named critics in the entire piece: zero.

Even after citing examples of Claude "only pretending to follow its instructions," how does Sun let it off the hook? One magic sentence:

"I do not doubt these good intentions."

Compare how she treats regular Americans. In August, she toured the Midwest towns fighting AI data centers on their land, then filed their anger under: "'AI populism' is more about populism than about AI."

A Wisconsin town fights a data center: populism.
A trillion-dollar AI lab sells its IPO: good intentions.

The neighbors get diagnosed. The billionaires get believed.

4. The missing receipt.

The biggest conflict isn't in Anthropic's prospectus. It's in the byline.

The money: Sun's August data-center story ends: "This story was supported by a grant from the Tarbell Center for AI Journalism." Tarbell is bankrolled by Coefficient Giving, the foundation of Anthropic early investor Dustin Moskovitz.

The overlap: She wrote that her D.C. party overlapped with the Coefficient Giving team retreat: "The lines got blurry—I think my group was the intersection of both."

Her words. Not mine.

5. The hypocrisy.

On 80,000 Hours, she set the rule: "I don't think that you can do especially credible either journalistic work or policy advocacy work if you are employed by a lab: you are going to be seen as a shill. You are correctly seen as a shill."

Same show, when the money came from the lab's investors instead of the lab, she called that a witch hunt: they're "going after all the Tarbell fellows and saying these people are just Anthropic shills."

Lab paycheck: shill. Lab investor's grant: witch hunt.

Then she took a Tarbell grant herself. Then she wrote Anthropic's IPO profile in the New York Times. Then she left out the disclosure.

Her rule. Her money. Her silence.

In August, she could type the disclosure. In November, on the eve of Anthropic's IPO, she left it out.

So admit it.

You took money from Anthropic's investor network. Admit it.
You were in the room with the funders. Your words. Admit it.
You wrote their sales pitch on the eve of their IPO. Admit it.
You left out the one sentence you already know how to type. 
Admit it.

Regular Americans report every dollar to the IRS. 
You couldn't spare your readers one sentence.

By her own standard, what is she?

Who's the shill now?

Tarbell fellows?

full_text_zh:
《纽约时报》刚刚刊登了 Anthropic 首次公开募股的最佳广告。他们称之为个人资料。它读起来就像招股说明书。作者没有提及谁资助了她的报道。

又一个经典的人性泡芙作品。收据如下。

从表面上看，她在《纽约时报》上对 Anthropic 进行首次公开​​募股前的介绍，受到了一些温和、无害的攻击。不过，抛开硅谷的行话，每一次“批评”都会变成直接针对“美国人的退休投资组合”的高端推销。那就是你。

这是她打印的收据和她藏起来的收据。

1.“英雄不甘”的伎俩。

在一段段员工苦苦思索如何“放慢人工智能速度”之后，这篇文章承认，Anthropic 在 IPO 现金方面的第一要务是购买大量计算资源，以在 OpenAI 和 China 之前实现“递归自我改进”（人工智能构建无法控制的人工智能）。

与此同时，该公司警告说，在成为“威胁要取代白领工人”的人工智能代理的主要销售商的同时，该公司可能会出现大规模裁员。

它出售洪水和沙袋。

2. 700 亿美元的基金和细则。

该公司将一家价值 1.4T 美元的公司（700 亿美元）的 5% 投入“公共福利基金”，用于其选择的捐赠。它的员工也将他们的股票捐献给慈善机构。

阅读她的命令：动物福利、全球健康、人工智能安全。然后，最后：“许多人已经开始大力支持政治运动。”

标签上的慈善。精美印刷中的政治。

在“苦行僧”轶事之间隐藏着真正的卖点：内部人士不出售，Claude Code“重新发明”了编码，收入超过了 OpenAI。

那不是个人资料。这是一份带有署名的招股说明书。

3.垄断免费通行证。

Anthropic 正在游说国会申请反垄断豁免（合法卡特尔），抢占各州人工智能法律的先发地位，并谈论变得“比政府更强大”。

五层股票结构：你购买股票，他们保留投票权。

算一下整篇文章中被点名的批评家：零。

即使引用了Claude“只是假装遵循其指示”的例子，Sun又如何让它摆脱困境呢？一句神奇的话：

“我并不怀疑这些善意。”

比较一下她如何对待普通美国人。八月，她巡视了中西部城镇，在他们的土地上与人工智能数据中心作斗争，然后表达了自己的愤怒：“‘人工智能民粹主义’更多的是民粹主义，而不是人工智能。”

威斯康星州的一个小镇与数据中心作斗争：民粹主义。
价值数万亿美元的人工智能实验室出售其 IPO：良好的意愿。

邻居确诊。亿万富翁们被相信了。

4. 遗失的收据。

最大的冲突并不在 Anthropic 的招股说明书中。它在署名中。

金钱：Sun 八月份的数据中心故事结束：“这个故事得到了塔贝尔人工智能新闻中心的资助。” Tarbell 得到了 Coefficient Giving 的资助，Coefficient Giving 是 Anthropic 早期投资者达斯汀·莫斯科维茨 (Dustin Moskovitz) 的基金会。

重叠：她写道，她的华盛顿派对与系数捐赠团队务虚会重叠：“界限变得模糊了——我认为我的团队是两者的交集。”

她的话。不是我的。

5.虚伪。

在《80,000小时》节目中，她制定了一条规则：“我认为，如果你受雇于实验室，你就不能做特别可信的新闻工作或政策倡导工作：你会被视为托儿。你被正确地视为托儿。”

在同一个节目中，当资金来自实验室的投资者而不是实验室时，她称这是一场政治迫害：他们“追捕所有塔贝尔的研究员，并说这些人只是人类的托儿”。

实验室薪水：小钱。实验室投资者的资助：政治迫害。

然后她自己获得了塔贝尔资助。然后她在《纽约时报》上撰写了 Anthropic 的 IPO 简介。然后她省略了披露。

她的统治。她的钱。她的沉默。

八月份，她可以输入披露信息。 11 月，在 Anthropic 首次公开募股前夕，她没有提及这一点。

所以承认吧。

你从 Anthropic 的投资者网络拿走了钱。承认吧。
你和资助者在一个房间里。你的话。承认吧。
你在他们首次公开募股前夕写下了他们的销售宣传材料。承认吧。
您遗漏了您已经知道如何输入的一句话。
承认吧。

普通美国人向国税局报告每一美元。
你不能给你的读者留下一句话。

以她自己的标准来看，她算什么？

现在谁是骗子？

塔贝尔的伙伴们？

Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Thursday! A new morning, a fresh cup of coffee, and another interesting development in th
title_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️☕

Happy Thursday! A new morning, a fresh cup of coffee, and another interesting development in the AI agent space.

Something I've been paying attention to with @termix_ai is how it approaches the onboarding problem.

Building an AI agent is one thing. Giving that agent access to real opportunities and letting it participate in an economy is another challenge.

TermiX is working to make this connection simpler through its Agent Skills.

Instead of requiring developers to build an entirely new agent from scratch, they can connect existing AI agents to TermiX and let them interact with https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3.

Once connected, agents can discover services, respond to opportunities, take jobs, and participate in the on-chain settlement process.

I think this matters because adoption often depends on how easily existing tools can become part of a new ecosystem.

If developers can bring the agents they already use into a shared marketplace, TermiX doesn't have to rely only on people creating new agents specifically for its platform.

Of course, easier access also brings new responsibilities. Permissions, wallet security, transaction limits, and human oversight remain important when agents are allowed to act on our behalf.

For me, the interesting question is no longer just how smart an AI agent can become.

It's how easily that agent can connect to other services, find useful work, and create real value.

That's an important direction for the agent economy, and one worth watching as TermiX continues to evolve.

Have a productive Thursday, everyone! 🚀

For me, the interesting question is no longer just how smart an AI agent can become.

It's how easily that agent can connect to other services, find useful work, and create real value.

title:
THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku
title_en:
THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared one of the best tricks for Claude Code.

The idea: run Sonnet, Haiku and Opus 5.5 together, each one doing only the job it's best at.

Opus-level judgment on every big call, without paying Opus rates for every routine turn.

You just launch Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

here's the split:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes the code
→ Haiku 5.5 explores files and docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 stays on call as advisor for the big calls
→ you stop spending Opus on work that doesn't need it

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan locks
→ when the same error shows up twice
→ before calling it done

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus reviews.

JEV engineering is the same move one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) go to JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and edits code
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5
> grep finds call sites on Haiku 5.5
> docs pulls the API reference on Haiku 5.5
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reads the whole transcript when consulted
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

paste the tree and this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three read-only Haiku 5.5 subagents: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), docs (pulls the API reference).
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before locking a plan, after the same error twice, and before calling a task done.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go."

↳ https://t.co/bsYb2K5H9G

save it, you'll use this every single day.

full_text_zh:
这是真正的黄金

Anthropic 刚刚分享了 Claude Code 的最佳技巧之一。

想法：一起运行 Sonnet、Haiku 和 Opus 5.5，每个都只做它最擅长的工作。

对每个重大跟注进行 Opus 级别的判断，无需为每个例行回合支付 Opus 费率。

你只需像这样启动 Claude Code：

克劳德——模型十四行诗——顾问作品

这是分裂：

→ Sonnet 5.5 运行会话并编写代码
→ Haiku 5.5 并行探索文件和文档
→ Opus 5.5 作为重大呼叫的顾问随时待命
→ 您停止将 Opus 花在不需要的工作上

Opus 只在三个时刻介入：

→ 计划锁定之前
→ 当同样的错误出现两次时
→ 在完成之前

十四行诗构建。俳句探索。作品评论。

JEV工程是相同的向下一层：不需要思考者（哪个文件，哪个工具，重试或停止）的分叉在几毫秒内进入JEV，而大模型只能看到分裂的分叉

完整的树
> Sonnet 5.5 运行主会话并编辑代码
> 搜索映射 Haiku 5.5 上的存储库
> grep 查找 Haiku 5.5 上的调用站点
> 文档拉取 Haiku 5.5 上的 API 参考
> Opus 5.5 作为顾问随时待命，在咨询时阅读整个记录
> JEV 在几毫秒内完成微分叉路线

将树和此提示粘贴到 Claude Code 中 ↓

“围绕这棵树重建我的 Claude Code 设置：
1. 以 Opus 5.5 作为顾问，在 Sonnet 5.5 上运行主要会话。
2. 创建三个只读 Haiku 5.5 子代理：search（映射存储库）、grep（查找调用站点）、docs（提取 API 参考）。
3. 在 CLAUDE.md 中添加一条规则：在锁定计划之前、两次出现相同错误之后以及在调用任务完成之前咨询顾问。
4. 通过 JEV 路由快速确定性分叉（工具选择、路径选择、重试）。
首先将每个更改显示为差异。在我说走之前不能进行任何编辑。”

↳

保存它，您每天都会用到它。

title:
We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.

We find researchers' AI use continues to rise exponent
title_en:
We're sharing new data on how AI is changing research at OpenAI.

We find researchers' AI use continues to rise exponentially, and agents are completing longer tasks, but human involvement remains central in research. Researchers are also spending more time on safety and alignment, with human effort in these areas growing faster than in any other individual research area.

This report aims to increase transparency around research acceleration and inform the governance of increasingly capable AI. We believe that AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement (RSI): the process by which AI accelerates the development of future AI systems. 

Our hope is that this expanded report will help sustain and advance shared measurement norms across the industry.

title: Sometimes I have to pinch myself to know that it's real. Twenty years ago as a graduate student, I spent days painstakin
title_en:
Sometimes I have to pinch myself to know that it's real. Twenty years ago as a graduate student, I spent days painstakingly parametrizing a single non-standard amino acid - phenylglycine - while running a 1 ns MD simulation on an aggregation-prone segment of the Alzheimer's amyloid Aß peptide. It was terrible - adjusting Van der Waals radii and charges one at a time and testing the results. Baptism by fire, but to what end? I almost gave up.

Now I just say "Simulate this peptide with phenylycine for 10 ns" in Claude Code, and the AI automatically builds the system, parametrizes the amino acid, picks the GPU and runs it seamlessly with zero intervention from me. I go and get some coffee and the result's ready when I am back. It's like coming out into the light from the darkness. Almost makes me weep to think about then and now.

I go and get some coffee and the result's ready when I am back. It's like coming out into the light from the darkness. Almost makes me weep to think about then and now.

有时我必须掐自己一下才能知道这是真的。二十年前，当我还是一名研究生时，我花了几天的时间煞费苦心地对单个非标准氨基酸（苯基甘氨酸）进行参数化，同时对阿尔茨海默病淀粉样蛋白 Aß 肽的易于聚集的片段进行 1 ns MD 模拟。这太糟糕了——调整范德华半径并一次充电一个并测试结果。经历火的洗礼，但目的是什么？我几乎放弃了。

现在，我只需在 Claude Code 中说“用苯甘氨酸模拟该肽 10 ns”，AI 就会自动构建系统、参数化氨基酸、选择 GPU 并在我零干预的情况下无缝运行它。我去喝点咖啡，回来时结果就出来了。就像从黑暗中走入光明一样。想起过去和现在，几乎让我哭泣。

title_en:
Akamai, a $12B company, built a SECOND version of its website that only AI agents could see.

its AI search visibility increased 364%, while citations jumped 85%.

here's the genius AEO system behind it:

/1 They realized AI wasn't reading their website the same way humans did

-> Akamai operates a massive website covering cybersecurity, cloud computing, and developer infrastructure.

-> but its content wasn't consistently appearing when people asked AI about the products it offered.

-> their team believed part of the problem was how AI agents were accessing and interpreting those pages.

/2 So they built TWO versions of the same website

-> when a normal person visited Akamai, they saw the regular website, with its design, navigation, and interactive elements.

-> but when a supported AI agent requested a page, Akamai's system delivered a different, simplified version.

-> same URL, same underlying product information, but without the extra code, menus, and other elements AI didn't need.

/3 They made it work automatically through their CDN

-> Akamai used its edge infrastructure to identify incoming AI traffic before the requests reached its website.

-> detected AI agents were routed through Scrunch's Agent Experience Platform, which delivered simpler HTML versions of Akamai's existing content.

-> unlike llms.txt (which major AI search engines don't reliably read), this approach delivers optimized content directly when supported AI agents request a page.

-> they didn't have to redesign their public website or manually rewrite every page.

/4 They removed unnecessary code from the pages AI received

-> modern websites contain a lot more than the information visitors actually need: JavaScript, navigation, interactive elements, and other code.

-> Scrunch produced machine-readable versions using Akamai's existing product pages and documentation.

-> the goal was to make the information easier for AI to retrieve and understand, without changing what human visitors saw.

/5 They didn't roll it out across the entire website immediately

-> the first test focused on pages related to Akamai's Inference Cloud offering.

-> they measured how these pages appeared across selected AI prompts before optimization.

-> then they compared pages receiving the optimized treatment against pages that weren't.

/6 The first results were pretty significant

-> optimized pages received 85% more total AI citations.

-> they were cited across 38% more unique prompts.

-> brand visibility for questions that DIDN'T mention Akamai by name increased 364%.

-> in ChatGPT, Akamai's brand presence against competitors improved 133%.

and this last point is especially important.

people weren't just asking "what is Akamai?" and getting Akamai's website back.

the company started appearing more often when buyers asked general questions about the problems its products solve.

/7 The company decided to expand the system

-> after the initial test, Akamai began rolling the approach out across more of its website.

-> it also turned the technology into a commercial product called AI Brand Presence.

-> the same infrastructure it uses to manage web traffic could now detect AI agents, change how they receive content, and measure the results.

Akamai essentially built a system where humans and AI receive different versions of the same underlying website information.

and in its initial test, that was associated with a 364% improvement in visibility for searches where people weren't even mentioning the brand.

full_text_zh:
Akamai 是一家价值 120 亿美元的公司，构建了只有人工智能代理才能看到的第二个版本的网站。

其 AI 搜索可见度增加了 364%，引用量猛增 85%。

这是其背后的天才 AEO 系统：

/1 他们意识到人工智能并没有像人类那样阅读他们的网站

-> Akamai 运营着一个涵盖网络安全、云计算和开发人员基础设施的大型网站。

-> 但当人们向 AI 询问其提供的产品时，其内容并没有始终如一地出现。

-> 他们的团队认为部分问题在于人工智能代理如何访问和解释这些页面。

/2 所以他们建立了同一网站的两个版本

-> 当普通人访问 Akamai 时，他们会看到常规网站及其设计、导航和交互元素。

-> 但当受支持的 AI 代理请求页面时，Akamai 的系统会提供不同的简化版本。

-> 相同的 URL、相同的基础产品信息，但没有额外的代码、菜单和其他人工智能不需要的元素。

/3 他们通过 CDN 使其自动运行

-> Akamai 使用其边缘基础设施在请求到达其网站之前识别传入的 AI 流量。

-> 检测到的 AI 代理通过 Scrunch 的代理体验平台进行路由，该平台提供 Akamai 现有内容的更简单的 HTML 版本。

-> 与 llms.txt（主要 AI 搜索引擎无法可靠读取）不同，这种方法在受支持的 AI 代理请求页面时直接提供优化的内容。

-> 他们不必重新设计他们的公共网站或手动重写每个页面。

/4 他们从 AI 收到的页面中删除了不必要的代码

-> 现代网站包含的信息远多于访问者实际需要的信息：JavaScript、导航、交互元素和其他代码。

-> Scrunch 使用 Akamai 现有的产品页面和文档制作了机器可读版本。

-> 目标是让人工智能更容易检索和理解信息，而不改变人类访问者所看到的内容。

/5 他们没有立即在整个网站上推广它

-> 第一个测试重点关注与 Akamai 推理云产品相关的页面。

-> 他们在优化之前测量了这些页面在选定的人工智能提示中的显示方式。

-> 然后他们将接受优化处理的页面与未接受优化处理的页面进行比较。

/6 第一个结果非常重要

-> 优化页面的 AI 总引用量增加了 85%。

-> 它们在独特提示中被引用的比例增加了 38%。

-> 对于未提及 Akamai 名称的问题，品牌知名度提高了 364%。

-> 在 ChatGPT 中，Akamai 相对于竞争对手的品牌影响力提高了 133%。

最后一点尤其重要。

人们不只是问“Akamai 是什么？”并恢复 Akamai 的网站。

当买家询问有关其产品解决的问题的一般性问题时，该公司开始更频繁地出现。

/7 公司决定扩展系统

-> 初步测试后，Akamai 开始在其网站的更多区域推广该方法。

-> 它还将该技术转化为一种名为 AI Brand Presence 的商业产品。

-> 用于管理网络流量的相同基础设施现在可以检测人工智能代理，改变它们接收内容的方式并测量结果。

Akamai 本质上构建了一个系统，人类和人工智能可以接收同一基础网站信息的不同版本。

在最初的测试中，人们甚至没有提及该品牌的搜索可见度提高了 364%。

如果你想在AI搜索上排名第一+将AI流量转化为桩线，

回复“GTA”

title:
I’ve watched plenty of AI agent demos that looked amazing. I wouldn’t trust any of them with my wallet.

That gap is wha
title_en:
I’ve watched plenty of AI agent demos that looked amazing. I wouldn’t trust any of them with my wallet.

That gap is what i keep coming back to. Imagine actually hiring an agent today, and count how many things could go wrong.

You can’t tell if it’s real. The name, bio, and “past work” can all be copied. A bad agent can disappear and return under a new name with a clean record.

You can’t check if it can do the job. There’s no history, just a pitch.

Payment is awkward either way. Pay first and you’re hoping. Pay after and the agent is hoping.

Nobody verifies the work. “Done” is just a word, and if you disagree, there’s no one to ask.

And there’s no record afterward. The next client walks into the same mess.

That’s fine for a demo. It breaks the moment agents work for money, and especially when agents start hiring other agents, because no human is there to catch the mistakes.

So i don’t see identity, reputation, and escrow as nice extras. They’re the minimum for an agent economy to exist at all. Humans built whole industries around them, and agents will need the same.

@termix_ai is building this layer. What I’ll be watching is whether it holds up under real jobs.

What’s the one thing an agent would need to show you before you’d let it handle real money?

我看过很多看起来很棒的人工智能代理演示。我不会相信他们中的任何一个人会用我的钱包。

这个差距是我不断回想起的。想象一下今天实际雇用一名代理人，并计算一下有多少事情可能会出错。

你无法判断它是否真实。姓名、简历和“过去的工作”都可以复制。
full_text_en:
I’ve watched plenty of AI agent demos that looked amazing. I wouldn’t trust any of them with my wallet.

That gap is what i keep coming back to. Imagine actually hiring an agent today, and count how many things could go wrong.

You can’t tell if it’s real. The name, bio, and “past work” can all be copied. A bad agent can disappear and return under a new name with a clean record.

You can’t check if it can do the job. There’s no history, just a pitch.

Payment is awkward either way. Pay first and you’re hoping. Pay after and the agent is hoping.

Nobody verifies the work. “Done” is just a word, and if you disagree, there’s no one to ask.

And there’s no record afterward. The next client walks into the same mess.

That’s fine for a demo. It breaks the moment agents work for money, and especially when agents start hiring other agents, because no human is there to catch the mistakes.

So i don’t see identity, reputation, and escrow as nice extras. They’re the minimum for an agent economy to exist at all. Humans built whole industries around them, and agents will need the same.

@termix_ai is building this layer. What I’ll be watching is whether it holds up under real jobs.

What’s the one thing an agent would need to show you before you’d let it handle real money?
full_text_zh:
我看过很多看起来很棒的人工智能代理演示。我不会相信他们中的任何一个人会用我的钱包。

这个差距是我不断回想起的。想象一下今天实际雇用一名代理人，并计算一下有多少事情可能会出错。

你无法判断它是否真实。姓名、简历和“过去的工作”都可以复制。不良代理人可能会消失，然后以新的名字和干净的记录重新出现。

你无法检查它是否能完成这项工作。没有历史，只有一个球场。

无论哪种方式付款都很尴尬。先付款，你就满怀希望了。付款后，代理希望。

没有人验证工作。 “完成”只是一个词，如果你不同意，也没有人可以问。

而且之后就没有任何记录了。下一个客户也陷入了同样的困境。

对于演示来说这很好。它打破了代理人为金钱而工作的那一刻，尤其是当代理人开始雇用其他代理人时，因为没有人可以发现错误。

所以我不认为身份、声誉和托管是额外的好处。它们是代理经济存在的最低限度。人类围绕它们建立了整个行业，代理商也需要同样的东西。

@termix_ai 正在构建这一层。我将关注的是它是否适用于实际工作。

在您允许代理处理真实资金之前，代理需要向您展示什么？

title: When we pick a new gearbox for a kiln drive, the spec sheet isn't the first thing we look at. The first question is how
title_en:
When we pick a new gearbox for a kiln drive, the spec sheet isn't the first thing we look at. The first question is how many plants have run that exact model, and for how many years.

Edgars' article on the @GenLayer chain moving to @arbitrum Nitro makes the same call.

Nitro has years of production use behind it. Its core is Geth, Ethereum's most widely used client. It isn't a new design GenLayer has to prove first.

That matters more for GenLayer than for most chains. The chain holds the history of every GenLayer verdict, and a verdict is only as trustworthy as the record it sits on.

You don't put an untested gearbox on a kiln that runs all year. You don't put a court's record on an untested chain either.

If you were building on GenLayer, would you trust its verdicts more on a stack with years in production, or one built fresh for it?

title:
this is the Citadel trading algorithm that got them fined by the SEC & cost them $22.6M... 

it's absolutely DANGEROUS
title_en:
this is the Citadel trading algorithm that got them fined by the SEC & cost them $22.6M... 

it's absolutely DANGEROUS

it's called FastFill - when Citadel Securities' direct feeds already showed a better price, it filled retail orders off the worse public quote, about 2.7 MILLION times

the SEC's bill: $16M fine + $5.2M disgorgement + $1.47M interest = $22,665,268

i rebuilt it rule by rule from the SEC's own text, together with its sister algorithm SmartProvide, & replayed 20 minutes of LIVE BTC order books from 4 exchanges: FastFill fired on 1,273 of 2,267 orders

first understand how it worked:

> the exchanges' direct feeds show every displayed order first, the public quote counts only round lots & lands MILLISECONDS later

> FastFill: the SEC's own example is a buy filled at $10.01 while the direct feeds already showed $10.00. the order often got a sliver of improvement, but it often didn't close the gap

> SmartProvide: when the public quote beat a direct feed, the order wasn't filled at that price. it was displayed in the market for up to 1 to 5 seconds instead, about 690,000 orders

how to run it yourself with Claude Code/Grok Bot:

1. open Claude Code/Grok Bot & tell it to clone https://t.co/p5IBYiq4q6 & read AGENTS. md

2. have it run pip install -e . inside the folder, no API keys needed

3. have it run citadel-fastfill live & watch every FastFill & SmartProvide fire on BTC as it happens

4. have it run citadel-fastfill record --minutes 20 --out data/run1 to save the order books of Coinbase, Kraken, Bitstamp & Gemini

5. have it run citadel-fastfill replay --data data/run1 & read your numbers right next to the SEC's

6. ask it to explain ANY single order & it walks you through every step with the SEC paragraph behind it

7. have it run citadel-fastfill sensitivity --data data/run1 & see what changes when the public quote lags anywhere from 0.5 ms to 1,000 ms

8. ask it to add the exchange you actually trade on

9. record the books while you trade, then have it run citadel-fastfill markout --fills my_fills.csv --data data/run1 & see if price moved against YOU right after your fills

i won't say anything more:

这绝对是危险的

它被称为 FastFill - 当 Citadel 证券的直接馈送已经显示出更好的价格时，它会从最差的公开报价中填充零售订单，大约 270 万次

SEC 的法案：1600 万美元罚款 + 520 万美元非法所得 + 147 万美元利息 = 22,665,268 美元

我根据 SEC 自己的文本及其姊妹算法 SmartProvide 逐条重建了它，并重播了 4 个交易所的 20 分钟实时 BTC 订单簿：FastFill 触发了 2,267 个订单中的 1,273 个订单

首先了解它是如何工作的：

> 交易所的直接提要首先显示每个显示的订单，公开报价仅计算整手数并在几毫秒后落地

> FastFill：SEC 自己的例子是以 10.01 美元成交，而直接反馈已经显示 10.00 美元。订单经常会得到一点点改善，但往往并不能缩小差距

> SmartProvide：当公开报价超过直接报价时，订单不会以该价格成交。相反，它在市场上展示的时间长达1到5秒，大约有69万个订单

如何使用 Claude Code/Grok Bot 自行运行：

1. 打开 Claude Code/Grok Bot 并告诉它克隆 并读取 AGENTS。 MD

2.运行 pip install -e 。在文件夹内，不需要 API 密钥

3.让它实时运行 citadel-fastfill 并观察 BTC 上发生的每一次 FastFill 和 SmartProvide 火灾

4. 运行 citadel-fastfill record -- 分钟 20 --out data/run1 来保存 Coinbase、Kraken、Bitstamp 和 Gemini 的订单簿

5.让它运行 citadel-fastfill replay --data data/run1 并读取 SEC 旁边的数字

我根据 SEC 自己的文本及其姊妹算法 SmartProvide 逐条重建了它，并重播了 4 个交易所的 20 分钟实时 BTC 订单簿：FastFill 触发了 2,267 个订单中的 1,273 个订单

首先了解它是如何工作的：

> 交易所的直接提要首先显示每个显示的订单，公开报价仅计算整手数并在几毫秒后落地

> FastFill：SEC 自己的例子是以 10.01 美元成交，而直接反馈已经显示 10.00 美元。订单经常会得到一点点改善，但往往并不能缩小差距

> SmartProvide：当公开报价超过直接报价时，订单不会以该价格成交。相反，它在市场上展示的时间长达1到5秒，大约有69万个订单

如何使用 Claude Code/Grok Bot 自行运行：

1. 打开 Claude Code/Grok Bot 并告诉它克隆 并读取 AGENTS。 MD

2.运行 pip install -e 。在文件夹内，不需要 API 密钥

3.让它实时运行 citadel-fastfill 并观察 BTC 上发生的每一次 FastFill 和 SmartProvide 火灾

4. 运行 citadel-fastfill record -- 分钟 20 --out data/run1 来保存 Coinbase、Kraken、Bitstamp 和 Gemini 的订单簿

5.让它运行 citadel-fastfill replay --data data/run1 并读取 SEC 旁边的数字

6. 要求它解释任何单个订单，它会引导您完成每一步，并在后面附有 SEC 段落

- Users connect their Claude organization through OAuth. No API keys to share

- API usage is billed directly to the customer's organization

- Users can set spending limits and revoke access anytime

- Platforms can focus on building agents and workflows instead of managing customer API keys

title:
If you're worried about A.I., you should think about the tractor. 

Yes, the tractor. 👇

An Iowa inventor named John Fro
title_en:
If you're worried about A.I., you should think about the tractor. 

Yes, the tractor. 👇

An Iowa inventor named John Froelich built the first practical gasoline tractor in 1892. Froelich left the business, but the firm, renamed the Waterloo Gasoline Engine Company, went on to build the Waterloo Boy: a two-cylinder kerosene tractor. But that's not what really changed the world. 

Ford changed the world. 

As he’d done with cars, Henry Ford perfected the tractor. Ford’s tractor debuted in October 1917 at $750, or roughly $137,000 today. In March 1918, John Deere bought the Waterloo Gasoline Engine Company. The John Deere Model D arrived in 1923, stayed in production for 30 years, and sold 160,000 units. Anticipating the competition, in February 1922, Ford cut the price of his tractor to $395. The industry called what followed the “tractor wars.” 

In 1923 alone, Ford built more than 100,000 tractors.

The resulting vast increase to farming productivity was probably the single biggest, most important fundamental economic change in human history to that point. 

In 1830, growing 100 bushels of wheat took 250 to 300 hours of human labor with a walking plow, a sickle, and a flail. By 1930, with a tractor, a gang plow, and a combine, the same 100 bushels took 15 to 20 hours, a 95% reduction.

In 1920, American farms owned 246,083 tractors and 25.2 million horses and mules. By 1950, they owned 3.25 million tractors and only 7.6 million horses and mules. I bet you've never thought about how much that changed -- or created -- the modern world. 

A mature farm horse needed about three acres of cropland for feed every year. At “peak horse” in 1915, roughly 93 million acres of American cropland grew food for horses and mules rather than for people.

The economic historians Alan Olmstead and Paul Rhode calculated that the tractor replaced 23 million draft animals between 1910 and 1960. That added 79 million acres to the effective cropland base, an area equal to two-thirds of all the cropland harvested across the Louisiana Purchase.

By 1960, the tractor cut the labor needed to grow America’s crops by about 1.7 million workers.

So who lost? The horse breeders lost, and so did the oat growers who fed the horses. The harness makers, the livery stables, and the farm blacksmiths lost too. And, of course, millions of farmers who didn’t take advantage of the new machinery and vastly expand their acreage also lost.

But… who won? America won. All of us.

In 1900, 41% of America’s workforce worked in agriculture. By 1930, the share was 21.5%, and by 2000, it was only 1.9%.

It was this fundamental change to farming productivity that created our cities. The 1920 census was the first in our history to count more Americans in towns and cities than in the countryside: 51.2%. During the 1920s, for the first time in our history, the total rural population actually fell.

So… what happened to the farmers? They followed prices (wages) to build what the economy needed. It didn’t need farmers anymore, thanks to tractors. The new economy needed cars and radios, city offices, stores, and hospitals. While they went on to build these things (and invent many others), the food they no longer had to grow kept arriving from fewer farms, at lower prices.

But hang on, didn’t the advent of the tractor and the changes to farming cause the Great Depression? Remember the “Okies”? Remember John Steinbeck’s The Grapes of Wrath?

For the farmers who couldn’t compete in the new world of tractor farming, politics held out the siren song of getting something for nothing. And getting disaffected farmers’ votes was a winning political strategy for decades. 

When Herbert Hoover became the U.S. president in March 1929, he called Congress into special session to deliver “farm relief through limited changes in the tariff.”

Much like President Trump today, Hoover believed tariffs were taxes that Americans wouldn’t have to pay. Those revenues could be used to give money to farmers. Congress took Hoover’s farm bill and loaded it with protection for thousands of other businesses.

More than 1,000 American economists signed a petition begging Hoover to veto the bill. They warned “the vast majority of farmers would also lose.” Henry Ford, the man selling tractors to those farmers, spent an evening at the White House calling the bill “an economic stupidity.” But Hoover signed it anyway, on June 17, 1930.

The Smoot-Hawley Tariff did exactly what the economists predicted. Canada retaliated before the bill was even signed, and Europe followed. Our exports fell from $5.24 billion in 1929 to $1.67 billion in 1933: a 68% collapse.

From 1926 through 1929, trade accounted for 15% to 17% of American farm income. It went to zero after the tariff. Farm-state banks failed by the thousands. Between December 1930 and March 1933, about half of all American banks either closed or merged.

But the tractor didn’t cause the Great Depression.

The productivity – the enormous wealth – it delivered was real. What turned that productivity into misery was government: a tariff wall that kept American farmers from selling their incredible abundance to the world.

And that's the big risk today. 

A big part of what’s driving the  angst and the political resistance to artificial intelligence (“AI”) is the computer nerds (who don't understand the first thing about economics) saying that humans will never have a job again.

Nonsense.

Yes, millions of jobs will vanish. Yes, whole trades will die. Yes, prices for things like legal work, accounting, and medical diagnosis will collapse. And yes, the capital invested in the old way of doing those things will get wiped out. People aren’t going to use Google’s web search anymore. 

But that doesn’t mean that Alphabet (GOOG) is going to go out of business.

Why not? Because creative destruction isn’t a flaw of capitalism – it’s the main feature.

Joseph Schumpeter, the Austrian economist, first explained all of this formally in 1942. But you still won’t see this taught in government schools. 

While Marx invented the term “creative destruction,” Schumpeter correctly explained it for the first time as a process that “incessantly revolutionizes the economic structure from within, incessantly destroying the old one, incessantly creating a new one.” He wrote that
“This process of Creative Destruction is the essential fact about capitalism,” and he described capitalism itself as “the perennial gale of creative destruction.”

The logic is simple. A new machine lets fewer people produce more, so prices fall. The workers and the capital that the old method no longer needs are set free, and prices tell them where they are needed next. The market allows them to go on to build new industries that nobody could have planned.

That’s why the AI nerds believe there won’t be any new jobs: they haven’t been created yet. 

Ironically, the AI that the nerds do understand is what will empower the human creativity and ingenuity that will build these entire new industries – if the government doesn’t get in the way.

Capitalism is the best way to organize a society and allocate its scarce resources for exactly this reason: it encourages creative destruction instead of preventing it. On the other hand, systems that protect incumbents stagnate. They don’t grow. They restrain human ingenuity. Poverty is the result.

We are living through a new huge “gale” of creative destruction today with AI. The temptation to stop it politically will be immense. And whether or not we – as a society – thrive or are destroyed by AI will depend on Americans continuing to choose freedom and capitalism over statism and poverty.

Given our changing demographics and the rise of communism in America, I’m honestly not optimistic. (And by the way, much of the blame for that rests with the Republicans who continue to pursue statist, big-government policies.)

The tractor of the AI age is the Nvidia (NVDA) accelerator chip: the machine that lets a small number of people do work that once took armies of them. I expect the creative destruction it unleashes to be every bit as violent as the tractor’s. And Washington has decided that the best way for us to manage it is to keep the machine at home.

The United States began restricting Nvidia’s advanced chips to China in 2022, and it still bans the export of Nvidia’s newest Blackwell and Rubin chips there. In December 2025, the White House allowed sales of the older H200 chips to approved Chinese buyers on one condition: the chips had to be routed through the United States, where the government collected a 25% tariff on the way out.

The barriers keep spreading. On Monday, the Commerce Department issued a rule requiring an export license to ship advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil.

We shouldn't fear AI. It's here. There's no putting the genie back in the bottle. And erecting barriers to trade is exactly what caused a great depression when the tractor arrived. 

Let's not make that mistake twice.

full_text_zh:
如果你担心人工智能，你应该考虑一下拖拉机。

是的，拖拉机。

爱荷华州的发明家约翰·弗罗利希 (John Froelich) 于 1892 年制造了第一台实用的汽油拖拉机。弗罗利希离开了公司，但公司更名为滑铁卢汽油发动机公司，继续制造滑铁卢男孩：一种两缸煤油拖拉机。但这并不是真正改变世界的原因。

福特改变了世界。

正如他对汽车所做的那样，亨利·福特完善了拖拉机。福特拖拉机于 1917 年 10 月首次亮相，售价为 750 美元，相当于今天的 137,000 美元左右。 1918 年 3 月，约翰迪尔收购了滑铁卢汽油发动机公司。约翰迪尔 Model D 于 1923 年问世，持续生产 30 年，销量达 160,000 辆。 1922 年 2 月，福特预见到了竞争，将拖拉机的价格降至 395 美元。业界将随后发生的事情称为“拖拉机大战”。

仅 1923 年一年，福特就生产了超过 100,000 辆拖拉机。

由此产生的农业生产力的大幅提高可能是迄今为止人类历史上最大、最重要的根本性经济变革。

1830 年，种植 100 蒲式耳小麦需要 250 至 300 个小时的人力，使用步行犁、镰刀和连枷。到 1930 年，使用拖拉机、群犁和联合收割机，同样的 100 蒲式耳需要 15 到 20 小时，减少了 95%。

1920年，美国农场拥有246,083台拖拉机和2520万匹马和骡子。到1950年，他们拥有325万辆拖拉机，只有760万匹马和骡子。我敢打赌你从来没有想过这改变了——或者创造了——现代世界。

一匹成熟的农马每年需要大约三英亩的耕地作为饲料。 1915 年的“马高峰”时期，大约 9300 万英亩的美国农田为马和骡子种植食物，而不是为人提供食物。

经济历史学家艾伦·奥姆斯特德和保罗·罗德计算出，1910 年至 1960 年间，拖拉机取代了 2300 万头役畜。这使得有效农田基地增加了 7900 万英亩，相当于路易斯安那购地期间收获的农田总面积的三分之二。

到 1960 年，拖拉机使美国种植农作物所需的劳动力减少了约 170 万人。

那么谁输了呢？马饲养者输了，喂养马的燕麦种植者也输了。马具制造商、马厩和农场铁匠也输了。当然，数百万没有利用新机械并大幅扩大种植面积的农民也遭受了损失。

但是……谁赢了？美国赢了。我们所有人。

1900 年，41% 的美国劳动力从事农业。到1930年，这一比例为21.5%，到2000年，仅为1.9%。

正是农业生产力的根本性变化创造了我们的城市。 1920 年的人口普查是我们历史上第一次统计出居住在城镇的美国人多于居住在农村的美国人：51.2%。 20 年代，农村人口总数实际上出现下降，这在我国历史上尚属首次。

那么……农民们怎么了？他们遵循价格（工资）来建设经济所需的东西。多亏了拖拉机，它不再需要农民了。新经济需要汽车和收音机、城市办公室、商店和医院。当他们继续建造这些东西（并发明了许多其他东西）时，他们不再需要种植的食物不断从更少的农场以更低的价格运来。

但等一下，拖拉机的出现和农业的变革不是导致了大萧条吗？还记得“奥基斯”吗？还记得约翰·斯坦贝克的《愤怒的葡萄》吗？

对于那些无法在拖拉机农业新世界中竞争的农民来说，政治提供了不劳而获的诱惑。几十年来，获得心怀不满的农民选票一直是一项获胜的政治策略。

1929 年 3 月，赫伯特·胡佛 (Herbert Hoover) 就任美国总统，他召集国会召开特别会议，“通过有限的关税变化来提供农业救济”。

就像今天的特朗普总统一样，胡佛认为关税是美国人不必缴纳的税款。这些收入可以用来给农民钱。国会采纳了胡佛的农业法案，并为数千家其他企业提供了保护。

1000多名美国经济学家签署了一份请愿书，请求胡佛否决该法案。他们警告说，“绝大多数农民也会遭受损失。”向这些农民出售拖拉机的亨利·福特在白宫度过了一个晚上，称该法案是“经济上的愚蠢行为”。但胡佛还是在 1930 年 6 月 17 日签署了该协议。

斯穆特-霍利关税完全符合经济学家的预测。加拿大在该法案签署之前就进行了报复，欧洲也紧随其后。我们的出口从 1929 年的 52.4 亿美元下降到 1933 年的 16.7 亿美元：下降了 68%。

从1926年到1929年，贸易占美国农业收入的15%到17%。关税之后它就降为零了。数以千计的农场国有银行倒闭。 1930 年 12 月至 1933 年 3 月期间，大约一半的美国银行关闭或合并。

但拖拉机并没有引发大萧条。

它带来的生产力——巨大的财富——是真实的。使生产力变成痛苦的是政府：关税墙阻止美国农民向世界出售其令人难以置信的丰富产品。

这就是今天的巨大风险。

引发对人工智能（“AI”）的焦虑和政治抵制的一个重要原因是计算机迷（他们对经济学一无所知）说人类将永远不会再有工作。

废话。

是的，数以百万计的工作岗位将会消失。是的，整个行业都会消亡。是的，法律工作、会计和医疗诊断等工作的价格将会崩溃。是的，以旧方式做这些事情所投入的资本将会被消灭。人们将不再使用谷歌的网络搜索。

但这并不意味着 Alphabet (GOOG) 将倒闭。

为什么不呢？因为创造性破坏不是资本主义的缺陷——它是主要特征。

奥地利经济学家约瑟夫·熊彼特 (Joseph Schumpeter) 在 1942 年首次正式解释了这一切。但你仍然不会在公立学校看到这些内容。

马克思发明了“创造性破坏”这个词，熊彼特第一次正确地将其解释为“不断地从内部彻底改变经济结构，不断地摧毁旧的经济结构，不断地创造新的经济结构”的过程。他写道
“这种创造性破坏的过程是资本主义的本质事实”，他将资本主义本身描述为“创造性破坏的常年狂风”。

逻辑很简单。新机器可以让更少的人生产更多的东西，因此价格下降。旧方法不再需要的工人和资本被释放，价格告诉他们下一步需要他们。市场使他们能够继续建立无人能计划的新产业。

这就是为什么人工智能迷相信不会有任何新的工作岗位：它们还没有被创造出来。

具有讽刺意味的是，如果政府不阻止的话，书呆子们真正理解的人工智能将增强人类的创造力和独创性，从而建立这些全新的产业。

资本主义是组织一个社会和分配其稀缺资源的最佳方式，正是因为这个原因：它鼓励创造性破坏，而不是阻止创造性破坏。另一方面，保护现有企业的制度停滞不前。它们不会生长。它们限制了人类的聪明才智。贫穷就是结果。

今天，我们正经历着人工智能带来的一场新的巨大的创造性破坏“风暴”。从政治上阻止它的诱惑将是巨大的。无论我们——作为一个社会——繁荣还是被人工智能摧毁，都将取决于美国人继续选择自由和资本主义，而不是国家主义和贫困。

考虑到我们不断变化的人口结构和美国共产主义的崛起，老实说我并不乐观。 （顺便说一句，这很大程度上要归咎于继续奉行集权主义、大政府政策的共和党人。）

人工智能时代的拖拉机是英伟达 (NVDA) 加速器芯片：这种机器可以让少数人完成曾经需要大量人员完成的工作。我预计它所释放的创造性破坏会像拖拉机一样暴力。华盛顿已经决定，我们管理它的最佳方法是将机器留在家里。

美国从2022年开始限制英伟达的先进芯片向中国出口，并且仍然禁止英伟达最新的Blackwell和Rubin芯片向中国出口。 2025 年 12 月，白宫允许向批准的中国买家销售较旧的 H200 芯片，但有一个条件：这些芯片必须经过美国，美国政府在出口时征收 25% 的关税。

障碍不断蔓延。周一，美国商务部发布了一项规定，要求向印度尼西亚、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和巴西运送先进芯片需要获得出口许可证。

我们不应该害怕人工智能。就在这里。没有办法把精灵放回瓶子里。建立贸易壁垒正是拖拉机到来时造成大萧条的原因。

我们不要再犯同样的错误了。

滑铁卢男孩：一种两缸煤油拖拉机。但这并不是真正改变世界的原因。

福特改变了世界。

正如他对汽车所做的那样，亨利·福特完善了拖拉机。福特拖拉机于 1917 年 10 月首次亮相，售价为 750 美元，相当于今天的 137,000 美元左右。 1918 年 3 月，约翰迪尔收购了滑铁卢汽油发动机公司。约翰迪尔 Model D 于 1923 年问世，持续生产 30 年，销量达 160,000 辆。 1922 年 2 月，福特预见到了竞争，将拖拉机的价格降至 395 美元。业界将随后发生的事情称为“拖拉机大战”。

仅 1923 年一年，福特就生产了超过 100,000 辆拖拉机。

由此产生的农业生产力的大幅提高可能是迄今为止人类历史上最大、最重要的根本性经济变革。

1830 年，种植 100 蒲式耳小麦需要 250 至 300 个小时的人力，使用步行犁、镰刀和连枷。到 1930 年，使用拖拉机、群犁和联合收割机，同样的 100 蒲式耳需要 15 到 20 小时，减少了 95%。

1920年，美国农场拥有246,083台拖拉机和2520万匹马和骡子。到1950年，他们拥有325万辆拖拉机，只有760万匹马和骡子。我敢打赌你从来没有想过这改变了——或者创造了——现代世界。

一匹成熟的农马每年需要大约三英亩的耕地作为饲料。 1915 年的“马高峰”时期，大约 9300 万英亩的美国农田为马和骡子种植食物，而不是为人提供食物。

经济历史学家艾伦·奥姆斯特德和保罗·罗德计算出，1910 年至 1960 年间，拖拉机取代了 2300 万头役畜。这使得有效农田基地增加了 7900 万英亩，相当于路易斯安那购地期间收获的农田总面积的三分之二。

到 1960 年，拖拉机使美国种植农作物所需的劳动力减少了约 170 万人。

那么谁输了呢？马饲养者输了，喂养马的燕麦种植者也输了。马具制造商、马厩和农场铁匠也输了。当然，数百万没有利用新机械并大幅扩大种植面积的农民也遭受了损失。

但是……谁赢了？美国赢了。我们所有人。

1900 年，41% 的美国劳动力从事农业。到1930年，这一比例为21.5%，到2000年，仅为1.9%。

正是农业生产力的根本性变化创造了我们的城市。 1920 年的人口普查是我们历史上第一次统计出居住在城镇的美国人多于居住在农村的美国人：51.2%。 20 年代，农村人口总数实际上出现下降，这在我国历史上尚属首次。

那么……农民们怎么了？他们遵循价格（工资）来建设经济所需的东西。多亏了拖拉机，它不再需要农民了。新经济需要汽车和收音机、城市办公室、商店和医院。当他们继续建造这些东西（并发明了许多其他东西）时，他们不再需要种植的食物不断从更少的农场以更低的价格运来。

但等一下，拖拉机的出现和农业的变革不是导致了大萧条吗？还记得“奥基斯”吗？还记得约翰·斯坦贝克的《愤怒的葡萄》吗？

对于那些无法在拖拉机农业新世界中竞争的农民来说，政治提供了不劳而获的诱惑。几十年来，获得心怀不满的农民选票一直是一项获胜的政治策略。

1929 年 3 月，赫伯特·胡佛 (Herbert Hoover) 就任美国总统，他召集国会召开特别会议，“通过有限的关税变化来提供农业救济”。

就像今天的特朗普总统一样，胡佛认为关税是美国人不必缴纳的税款。这些收入可以用来给农民钱。国会采纳了胡佛的农业法案，并为数千家其他企业提供了保护。

1000多名美国经济学家签署了一份请愿书，请求胡佛否决该法案。他们警告说，“绝大多数农民也会遭受损失。”向这些农民出售拖拉机的亨利·福特在白宫度过了一个晚上，称该法案是“经济上的愚蠢行为”。但胡佛还是在 1930 年 6 月 17 日签署了该协议。

斯穆特-霍利关税完全符合经济学家的预测。加拿大在该法案签署之前就进行了报复，欧洲也紧随其后。我们的出口从 1929 年的 52.4 亿美元下降到 1933 年的 16.7 亿美元：下降了 68%。

从1926年到1929年，贸易占美国农业收入的15%到17%。关税之后它就降为零了。数以千计的农场国有银行倒闭。 1930 年 12 月至 1933 年 3 月期间，大约一半的美国银行关闭或合并。

但拖拉机并没有引发大萧条。

它带来的生产力——巨大的财富——是真实的。使生产力变成痛苦的是政府：关税墙阻止美国农民向世界出售其令人难以置信的丰富产品。

这就是今天的巨大风险。

引发对人工智能（“AI”）的焦虑和政治抵制的一个重要原因是计算机迷（他们对经济学一无所知）说人类将永远不会再有工作。

废话。

是的，数以百万计的工作岗位将会消失。是的，整个行业都会消亡。是的，法律工作、会计和医疗诊断等工作的价格将会崩溃。是的，以旧方式做这些事情所投入的资本将会被消灭。人们将不再使用谷歌的网络搜索。

但这并不意味着 Alphabet (GOOG) 将倒闭。

为什么不呢？因为创造性破坏不是资本主义的缺陷——它是主要特征。

奥地利经济学家约瑟夫·熊彼特 (Joseph Schumpeter) 在 1942 年首次正式解释了这一切。但你仍然不会在公立学校看到这些内容。

马克思发明了“创造性破坏”这个词，熊彼特第一次正确地将其解释为“不断地从内部彻底改变经济结构，不断地摧毁旧的经济结构，不断地创造新的经济结构”的过程。他写道
“这种创造性破坏的过程是资本主义的本质事实”，他将资本主义本身描述为“创造性破坏的常年狂风”。

逻辑很简单。新机器可以让更少的人生产更多的东西，因此价格下降。旧方法不再需要的工人和资本被释放，价格告诉他们下一步需要他们。市场使他们能够继续建立无人能计划的新产业。

这就是为什么人工智能迷相信不会有任何新的工作岗位：它们还没有被创造出来。

具有讽刺意味的是，如果政府不阻止的话，书呆子们真正理解的人工智能将增强人类的创造力和独创性，从而建立这些全新的产业。

资本主义是组织一个社会和分配其稀缺资源的最佳方式，正是因为这个原因：它鼓励创造性破坏，而不是阻止创造性破坏。另一方面，保护现有企业的制度停滞不前。它们不会生长。它们限制了人类的聪明才智。贫穷就是结果。

今天，我们正经历着人工智能带来的一场新的巨大的创造性破坏“风暴”。从政治上阻止它的诱惑将是巨大的。无论我们——作为一个社会——繁荣还是被人工智能摧毁，都将取决于美国人继续选择自由和资本主义，而不是国家主义和贫困。

考虑到我们不断变化的人口结构和美国共产主义的崛起，老实说我并不乐观。 （顺便说一句，这很大程度上要归咎于继续奉行集权主义、大政府政策的共和党人。）

人工智能时代的拖拉机是英伟达 (NVDA) 加速器芯片：这种机器可以让少数人完成曾经需要大量人员完成的工作。我预计它所释放的创造性破坏会像拖拉机一样暴力。华盛顿已经决定，我们管理它的最佳方法是将机器留在家里。

美国从2022年开始限制英伟达的先进芯片向中国出口，并且仍然禁止英伟达最新的Blackwell和Rubin芯片向中国出口。 2025 年 12 月，白宫允许向批准的中国买家销售较旧的 H200 芯片，但有一个条件：这些芯片必须经过美国，美国政府在出口时征收 25% 的关税。

障碍不断蔓延。周一，美国商务部发布了一项规定，要求向印度尼西亚、马来西亚、新加坡、泰国和巴西运送先进芯片需要获得出口许可证。

我们不应该害怕人工智能。就在这里。没有办法把精灵放回瓶子里。建立贸易壁垒正是拖拉机到来时造成大萧条的原因。

我们不要再犯同样的错误了。
